candidates.claim: iter_billing_days now loops while day < end, but end is inclusive (see the docstring and the old range(... + 1)). The last day of every period is dropped, so prorate undercharges: a full January bills 30/31 of the fee.

apply_discount now does the arithmetic in binary floats and rounds with round(), which is round-half-even on an inexact value. Half-cent results no longer round half-up as to_money does, so invoices can be a cent short.
candidates.trigger: apply_discount(Decimal('1.15'), 50): exact result 0.575 should round half-up to 0.58

candidates.claim: Invoice.subtotal now uses sum() over a generator. For an invoice with no lines, sum() returns the int 0 rather than a Decimal, so code that quantizes or formats the subtotal breaks.

prove/C1/attempt-1.reasoning: January 2026 has 31 days. Prorating 1-31 January covers every day, so the full monthly fee is due. With the off-by-one only 30 days are counted and the result is 30.00.
prove/C1/attempt-1.test_code:
from datetime import date
from decimal import Decimal

from invoicing.dates import prorate


def test_full_month_is_charged_in_full() -> None:
    # 1-31 January is the whole month, both ends inclusive: the full fee is due.
    assert prorate(Decimal("31.00"), date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 1, 31)) == Decimal("31.00")
